issues.title: Habigoal: Build a coach command center with a daily priority athlete queue
issues.objective: Turn the home experience into a real coach operating surface that highlights who needs attention first.
issues.context: Catapult, AthleteMonitoring, WHOOP Unite, and Smartabase all centralize athlete status into a staff-facing operational picture instead of leaving coaches to inspect one athlete at a time.
issues.goal: Give coaches one daily queue for priority athletes, missed check-ins, low-readiness cases, and unresolved support flags.
acceptance: home dashboard ranks athletes by actionable urgency
queue reasons are visible and understandable
coach can open an athlete profile directly from each queue item

issues.title: Habigoal: Add a custom wellness and check-in questionnaire builder
issues.objective: Make readiness capture adaptable without code changes.
issues.context: AthleteMonitoring and CoachMePlus both expose highly configurable forms and questionnaires so teams can tailor what they collect to their environment.
issues.goal: Allow staff to add, remove, reorder, and tune daily check-in prompts and response scales from settings.
acceptance: staff can create and edit question sets without redeploying
question changes preserve historical responses
the athlete flow renders configured questions correctly

issues.title: Habigoal: Add reminders, alerts, and missed check-in escalation
issues.objective: Raise compliance and shorten the time between a missed signal and coach follow-up.
issues.context: AthleteMonitoring, Catapult AMS, and CoachMePlus all use alerts and reminders to keep staff informed and athletes responsive.
issues.goal: Automate nudges for incomplete check-ins and alert staff on meaningful readiness or health thresholds.
acceptance: missed check-ins trigger reminders
high-risk responses trigger staff alerts
staff can configure timing and thresholds

issues.title: Habigoal: Build a wearable and device integrations hub
issues.objective: Increase signal quality by combining self-report with passive data.
issues.context: Catapult, Smartabase, CoachMePlus, AthleteMonitoring, WHOOP, and TrainingPeaks all emphasize device connectivity as a core value driver.
issues.goal: Create a clean ingestion model for device-derived sleep, recovery, HRV, heart rate, strain, and external-load data.
acceptance: platform can store device-derived daily metrics
metrics are normalized into a common schema
staff can see integration health and last sync state

issues.title: Habigoal: Add external and internal training-load monitoring
issues.objective: Move from wellbeing snapshots to full readiness-plus-load interpretation.
issues.context: Catapult and AthleteMonitoring are strong on load management, while TrainingPeaks and WHOOP show how load influences readiness and recovery.
issues.goal: Track session RPE, duration, workload trends, and simple acute-versus-recent load interpretation.
acceptance: coach can log or import session load
system shows short-term versus baseline load changes
load trends appear alongside readiness trends

issues.title: Habigoal: Add sleep, HRV, strain, and recovery trend interpretation
issues.objective: Make recovery signals more actionable across days and weeks.
issues.context: WHOOP Unite and TrainingPeaks both surface readiness through trend interpretation rather than one-day raw numbers alone.
issues.goal: Support a recovery layer that can incorporate sleep quality, HRV, strain, and recovery-derived metrics with plain-language interpretation.
acceptance: daily and rolling views exist for recovery metrics
coach sees plain-language interpretation
recovery trends can influence readiness summaries

issues.title: Habigoal: Build individual athlete trend dashboards with 7, 30, and custom windows
issues.objective: Improve staff pattern recognition over time.
issues.context: WHOOP Unite explicitly supports daily, 7-day, 30-day, and custom trend windows for individual members.
issues.goal: Let staff inspect the athlete’s history over short and medium windows without leaving the athlete page.
acceptance: athlete pages support multiple time windows
key readiness metrics can be compared over time
custom range filtering works across the trend views

issues.title: Habigoal: Build a team readiness summary with traffic-light action buckets
issues.objective: Help coaches understand team state at a glance before training starts.
issues.context: Industry leaders consistently provide team dashboards that compress many athlete signals into an operational team picture.
issues.goal: Group athletes into ready, watch, and support buckets with team-level rollups and counts.
acceptance: coaches can see team counts by bucket
bucket logic is transparent
coach can drill from bucket to athletes

issues.title: Habigoal: Add participation and availability management
issues.objective: Tie support signals to training participation decisions.
issues.context: Kitman Labs highlights participation management and availability as a distinct workflow for deciding whether activity should be limited, modified, or avoided.
issues.goal: Track athlete availability states and recommended participation level for each session day.
acceptance: staff can set and update availability states
availability is visible in daily coach views
state changes are preserved historically

issues.title: Habigoal: Add injury, illness, and mental health event tracking
issues.objective: Expand from readiness snapshots into support event management.
issues.context: AthleteMonitoring explicitly supports illness, injury, and mental health surveillance and central record keeping for health events.
issues.goal: Track support-relevant health events without forcing teams into a full medical-record product on day one.
acceptance: staff can log injury, illness, and mental health events
event status can be updated over time
event visibility can be controlled by role

issues.title: Habigoal: Build a return-to-play and return-to-participation workflow
issues.objective: Provide a structured recovery progression instead of ad hoc notes.
issues.context: AthleteMonitoring and other AMS platforms treat return-to-play as a distinct workflow tied to health status and training modification.
issues.goal: Support staged progression back into training after injury or illness.
acceptance: staff can define or use staged RTP steps
athlete status reflects current stage
the progression is visible in the athlete timeline

issues.title: Habigoal: Add growth and maturation tracking for youth athletes
issues.objective: Build a truly youth-athlete-specific decision layer.
issues.context: Kitman Labs explicitly positions growth and maturation monitoring as part of athlete development and training optimization.
issues.goal: Track maturation-adjacent data points and show their relevance to training load and support decisions.
acceptance: platform can record youth development metrics
trends can be reviewed over time
coaches receive clear contextual guidance instead of raw numbers only

issues.title: Habigoal: Add a testing and evaluation library
issues.objective: Make the platform useful beyond daily check-ins.
issues.context: TeamBuildr, CoachMePlus, AthleteMonitoring, and Smartabase all support evaluations or testing workflows as part of athlete development.
issues.goal: Store repeatable testing protocols and track athlete progress against them.
acceptance: staff can define test templates
results can be recorded and reviewed historically
athlete progress can be benchmarked over time

issues.title: Habigoal: Build a session planning calendar
issues.objective: Connect readiness to the actual planned week.
issues.context: TrainingPeaks is especially strong because planning, execution, and review happen on a visible calendar.
issues.goal: Show planned sessions, key events, and readiness context in one coach planning surface.
acceptance: coaches can create and view planned sessions
session planning is visible alongside readiness context
athlete or group views reflect the planned calendar

issues.title: Habigoal: Add secure coach-athlete messaging and support nudges
issues.objective: Let support actions happen inside the platform instead of outside it.
issues.context: CoachMePlus and TeamBuildr both emphasize integrated communication between coaches and athletes.
issues.goal: Enable direct messaging and templated support nudges tied to readiness context.
acceptance: coaches can send direct support messages
nudges can be triggered from athlete state
message history remains attached to the athlete context

issues.title: Habigoal: Build a parent and guardian summary mode
issues.objective: Add trust-building communication for youth environments.
issues.context: Most elite AMS tools are weak on youth family communication; this is a strong differentiation opportunity for Habigoal.
issues.goal: Provide a parent-safe summary view that explains support direction without exposing the full internal staff workflow.
acceptance: staff can generate a guardian-safe summary
sensitive notes remain hidden from guardians
guardian mode uses plain supportive language

issues.title: Habigoal: Build a recommendation engine for the next best support action
issues.objective: Turn monitoring into decision support.
issues.context: WHOOP uses behavioral insights, while leading AMS platforms use alerts and analytics; Habigoal should translate signals into concrete support suggestions.
issues.goal: Generate one or more next-best support actions from readiness, trend, and load context.
acceptance: system generates actionable suggestions
each suggestion explains why it was shown
coaches can review or dismiss suggestions

issues.title: Habigoal: Add session blueprint suggestions based on readiness state
issues.objective: Bridge the gap between athlete status and practice design.
issues.context: TrainingPeaks and load-management tools are valuable because they influence what happens next, not just what happened before.
issues.goal: Translate readiness states into practical session blueprints such as green, modified, or recovery.
acceptance: each readiness state maps to a session suggestion
coaches can see suggested modifications quickly
session blueprints are reusable across team planning

issues.title: Habigoal: Add customizable dashboard widgets and saved coach views
issues.objective: Support different workflows without building separate products for each staff role.
issues.context: AthleteMonitoring and CoachMePlus both emphasize customization of dashboards and analytics for different organizations.
issues.goal: Allow staff to configure what appears on their dashboards and save named views.
acceptance: staff can choose and arrange dashboard modules
saved views persist
views can be tailored by role or context

issues.title: Habigoal: Build a notes, files, and support evidence library
issues.objective: Keep support context attached to the athlete instead of scattered across tools.
issues.context: CoachMePlus and AthleteMonitoring both support storing documents, media, and records alongside athlete workflows.
issues.goal: Store support notes, files, and evidence artifacts directly in the athlete workspace.
acceptance: staff can attach files and notes to athletes
records appear in the athlete timeline
library access follows role permissions

issues.title: Habigoal: Add role-based permissions and privacy controls
issues.objective: Make the platform safe for broader school and club adoption.
issues.context: Kitman Labs, CoachMePlus, WHOOP Unite, and AthleteMonitoring all emphasize permissions, privacy, and controlled access.
issues.goal: Provide fine-grained access controls across coaches, medical staff, admins, and guardians.
acceptance: roles can be defined and assigned
sensitive data can be hidden by role
guardian-facing surfaces remain separate from internal staff data

issues.title: Habigoal: Add PDF and shareable operational reports
issues.objective: Make the platform useful in handoff, review, and communication contexts.
issues.context: Existing platforms provide reports because staff still need artifacts for meetings, decisions, and stakeholder communication.
issues.goal: Expand report generation from static exports into a reusable operational reporting layer.
acceptance: staff can generate athlete and team summaries
reports are structured for sharing
exports preserve the product’s core readiness narrative

issues.title: Habigoal: Build data import, export, and analytics connectors
issues.objective: Keep Habigoal interoperable with real-world staff toolchains.
issues.context: Smartabase and CoachMePlus both stress import and export flexibility, while Smartabase’s official case studies explicitly mention downstream analytics in R, Python, Tableau, and Power BI.
issues.goal: Support CSV import/export plus analytics-friendly downstream access patterns.
acceptance: staff can import structured data into the platform
exports are reliable and documented
external analytics workflows can consume Habigoal data cleanly

issues.title: Habigoal: Add a custom formulas and algorithm engine
issues.objective: Let organizations adapt scoring and thresholds to their methodology.
issues.context: CoachMePlus explicitly exposes an algorithm engine, and AthleteMonitoring emphasizes custom formulas, standards, and benchmarks.
issues.goal: Support configurable derived metrics, thresholds, and score formulas without code changes for every organization.
acceptance: staff can define derived calculations
formula output can power alerts and dashboards
invalid formulas are blocked safely

issues.title: Habigoal: Build tablet and kiosk capture mode for team check-ins
issues.objective: Reduce daily friction where athletes check in at the facility rather than individually at home.
issues.context: TeamBuildr’s tablet mode and AthleteMonitoring’s tablet capture workflows show that shared-device capture increases practical compliance in team environments.
issues.goal: Support a kiosk-style mode for sequential athlete check-ins on shared devices.
acceptance: shared-device mode supports multiple athletes in sequence
data remains private between athlete turns
coaches can monitor completion during the session window
